takeaways: Barrick posted $0.82 adjusted EPS vs $0.79 expected, but revenue of $5.07 billion came in just under the $5.13 billion consensus (StreetInsider).
It produced 816,000 ounces of gold, up 3% from Q2 and down 2% from a year ago; adjusted net earnings rose 37% y/y to $1.35 billion on higher gold prices (Investing.com).
All-in sustaining costs for gold rose to $1,911 an ounce from $1,538 a year ago, on lower ore grades, higher royalties and diesel.
Gold and copper guidance were reiterated, and the quarterly dividend is $0.175 a share.
verdict: Barrick beat on EPS and missed on revenue by a hair, and costs per ounce are climbing like gold itself. It is a gold miner: the gold price writes the plot, the company just digs. Max says shiny, but pricey to dig.
